result.answer: {"outcome":"diagnosed","finding":"permission_blocked","answer":"The failure is not a read-only session or transaction. The single host-authorized observation shows the connection reports query_only=0 (writable session state) and a read (row_count=1) succeeds, yet the prior INSERT still failed with SQLite error 8 'attempt to write a readonly database'. With query_only=0 ruled out, the read-only condition sits at the file/storage layer: the database file (or its containing directory, which SQLite needs for the journal/WAL) is not writable by the connecting process — i.e., an OS-level write permission block, not transaction read-only mode, not file corruption and not a lost mount. Evidence gap: this single bounded reading cannot distinguish directory-level write permission from a read-only mount of the same path; separating those two would need a further authorized check, which the readonly adapter does not provide. Consequently no recovery is demonstrated — the observation is diagnostic only.
